newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty slips as some foreigners sell Polish paper.
newsitem.headline: Zloty slips as some foreigners sell Polish paper.

text.p: The zloty eased against the basket in early Tuesday trade as shorter-term foreign investors sold Polish treasuries in secondary trade and dealers said the local currency could ease further later today.

"The zloty is sinking as foreigners exit and search for zlotys, and the unit could ease further," said Mateusz Bieniek of Societe Generale in Warsaw. "It's a question of supply and demand, and presently demand for zlotys is low," he added.
Dealers said however that foreign investors were not making any large-scale withdrawls from Polish treasuries and that there were also foreign players looking to enter the market.
"Trade is two-way with foreigners both buying and selling and this situation is likely to remain for some time," said Robert Gluch, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
At 0815 GMT the zloty was at 2.43/2.38 percent from parity, down from openings' 2.47/2.43 and Monday's 2.53/2.43 close.
It was at 3.1450/70 to the dollar and at 1.8611/19 to the mark, against opening's 3.1480/00 and 1.8569/74.

Dealers said that some foreign investors may have decided to sell Polish paper after it became apparant that the central bank would not allow the zloty to strenghten past 2.5 percent from parity in the near-term.
On the secondary market T-bill yields stabilized around average yield levels from Monday's primary tender.
Dealers said that 13-week paper, sold yesterday at 20.78 percent, was quoted at 20.80/72 percent.
They said that 26- and 52-week paper was around 21.35/30 percent, against Monday's avereage yield levels of 21.34 and 21.37 percent respectively.

On the money market overnight rates slipped below 22 percent as banks had cash surpluses despite monthly tax payment outflows, dealers said. At 0830 GMT O/N rates were at 21.70/21.90 percent against opening's 21.90/22.00 percent.
Tomorrow/next rates held flat at 21.85/22.15 percent.
The central bank was expected to stage a small 100 or 200 million zloty NBP-bill sale or refrain from money market operations on Tuesday, dealers said.
